question: Should editor exports and DOM contracts use neutral names across the Plate facade and its runtime, and which public nouns should disappear instead of being renamed?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; first-principles; maximum-value hard-cut; source-backed independent DOM subtask
trigger: User requested no Plite/Plate branding in public exports, preferred Editor vocabulary, and asked whether DOM attributes should become data-editor names.
requirements: Teach one public Plate API without exposing the internal distribution name in exported symbols and ordinary DOM hooks.
Prefer precise neutral domain nouns and preserve distinct model, mounted view, passive provider, plugin and copied-composition jobs.
Preserve generic inference, exact shared API identity and entrypoint dependency isolation.
Preserve registered-view ownership, nested editor and Shadow DOM behavior, native selection, repair, CSS hooks and static/live DOM correspondence.
Preserve exact clipboard and authored-document payloads across any supported interchange migration; do not mistake wire literals for transient DOM attributes.
Assessment only: no product implementation, new runtime machinery, publication or wholesale namespace migration is authorized by the review.
evidenceReuse: Extends the 2026-09-12 Plate docs audit into the public source naming question. Rechecked current exports, React owner collisions, copied callers, DOM ownership/repair and wire codecs. The existing plate-api scope addresses capability identity and its adopted implementation, not these names; this initial distinct question leaves that conclusion intact. Documentation-only naming debt is reaffirmed; the current proposal expands the desired neutral target to both brand families.
summary: Pursue neutral source-owned public names and one data-editor DOM contract; delete unnecessary markers and avoid mechanical Editor prefixes or per-layer aliases. Resolve React/provider/plugin collisions and treat wire names as data migrations.
alternatives: Keep/configure: hiding brand names in prose fails because exports, inferred declarations, copied source and CSS still expose the internal layer.
Change existing API: rename neutral shared declarations at their runtime owner and directly expose them through Plate; use Editor only where it clarifies the job.

Delete/merge/inline: cut unnecessary public internals and test-only DOM markers first. Remove the announcer marker in favor of its existing accessibility contract; path/key repair fallbacks are not proven removable. Provider/model/view roles must be resolved before naming.

Move ownership: keep neutral DOM selection/repair contracts at the runtime owner, Plate product declarations at Plate, and visual composition at copied UI. Reject Plate-only export aliases and dual DOM emission.

Add primitive: no new state, adapter registry, configurable prefix or provider is justified by naming. Existing private bindings are adequate ownership facts; exact attribute classification belongs in the current repair observer.

Replace architecture: removing all DOM hooks or the runtime package would destroy styling/custom-renderer/interchange jobs or change ownership without benefit proved by this request. Any private-lookup replacement needs separate behavior and applicable scale evidence.

Mechanical replacement: making every symbol Editor-prefixed preserves redundant nouns and creates React/provider/copied-component collisions. Clipboard and authored HTML strings require codec-specific migration, not a global substitution.
proofLimits: Current-source review and a bounded independent DOM source review only. Existing focused tests were located, not run. No browser, packed-export, inference, performance or wire-migration pass is claimed. Naming reuses the existing runtime; replacement lookup machinery is not accepted. Baseline global review-ledger check already fails on unrelated stale registry/blocks inventory; the new record is separately validated and source-fingerprinted.
